items.ground_truth_summary: Reject equivalence: porosity is a volume fraction, while permeability measures flow capacity and depends on connectivity.

items.source_locator: Rock and Fluid Properties; Darcy definition
items.ground_truth_summary: One darcy passes 1-cP fluid at 1 cm3/s through 1 cm2 under 1 atm/cm pressure gradient.

Reject saturation sum above one for the same two-phase pore volume; So + Sw equals one.

items.source_locator: Water displacement of oil; relative permeability
items.ground_truth_summary: As water saturation rises, oil relative permeability falls and water relative permeability rises.
Reject co-increase premise: oil kr decreases while water kr increases during water displacement.
Non-wetting pressure first exceeds entry pressure of largest pores; displaced wetting volume maps pore volume by threshold.
The four methods are porous diaphragm, centrifuge, dynamic capillary pressure, and mercury injection.
Pressure declines at the same rate everywhere, with zero flow at the outer drainage boundary.
Bubble point is first gas bubble; bubble gas is light-component enriched while liquid remains near overall composition.
Reject dew/bubble confusion: first liquid drop is dew-point language; bubble point is first gas bubble from liquid.
Solution-gas drive begins at bubble point as gas leaves solution and expands to drive oil.
Gas-cap drive has initial free gas at reservoir top; solution-gas drive starts undersaturated without an initial gas cap.
Support comes from aquifer expansion or artesian/outcrop recharge; relative aquifer size and water mobility are key.
Reject single-drive premise: many reservoirs combine gas-cap and water-drive energy.
Decline curves use rate versus time/cumulative withdrawal, largely neglect pressure, and change with operating mode.

Bg is same-mass gas volume at reservoir T,P divided by volume at standard conditions.
